subject: Consolidated observability pack — retention, tracing & dashboard seat model
messages:
From: Miguel Alvarez <miguel@brightsail.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability pack — retention / tracing questions

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We liked the advanced dashboards and the tracing UX, but before we move to an internal PoC we need clarity on two things:

1) Retention pricing: we expect a mix of hot (30d) and cold (12mo) spans — can you outline how credits vs slab pricing would apply for a 200k spans/day profile?
2) Dashboard seat vs ingestion model: our SREs want per-seat dashboard features for on-call — how does that map to your proposed bundle?

Our procurement lead also asked about a pilot discount and whether Redwood can cap surge costs for the first 90 days.

Attached is a small sample of our retention distribution (retention-sample-usage.csv). Can Kimberly or someone from pricing put together a short scenario matrix we can present to our CFO?

Cheers,
Miguel
Head of Platform — BrightSail AI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Miguel Alvarez <miguel@brightsail.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability pack — retention / tracing questions

Miguel —

Thanks for the sample. Quick answers up front, then we can follow with a short spreadsheet:

- Retention pricing: We offer two main ways to consume observability retention: a credits-first slab (best for predictable, steady ingest) or a metered token model (better if you expect spikes). For 200k spans/day with your 80/20 hot/cold split, the credits path typically saves ~18–25% vs pay-as-you-go because cold retention is amortized. I’ll attach a worked example.
- Dashboard seats: We decouple the advanced dashboard feature set (alerts, graphing, granular RBAC) from ingestion. Seats are licensed per active dashboard user; ingestion is billed separately. For BrightSail’s SRE team (7 active users) the seat cost is modest compared to ingestion for high-cardinality tracing.

Pilot concession: We can offer a 50% pilot credit on observability add-ons for 90 days, with a surge cap (not to exceed 150% of the forecasted spend) if you commit to a 6-month pilot contract. I’ve looped in Kimberly to formalize numbers.

Next step: Kimberly — can you draft 2 scenario rows (credits slab vs metered) and include a capped-concession line? I’ll send over a short SOW stub for legal review afterwards.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachment: BRIGHTSIL-OBS-pricing_v1.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Miguel Alvarez <miguel@brightsail.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability pack — retention / tracing questions

Miguel —

Attached is the scenario matrix you requested (BRIGHTSIL-OBS-pricing_v1.pdf). High-level notes:

- Scenario A (Credits slab): Assumes committed monthly credit of 5M retention units. With your sample distribution, this maps to ~22% lower unit cost for cold spans and 15% lower for hot spans vs the metered model.
- Scenario B (Metered + seat license): No commit, billed monthly. Easier to start, but at your projected 200k spans/day we estimate a 14% higher 6-month spend vs Scenario A.
- Pilot concession: 50% credits back for 90 days, applied as a one-time invoice credit. Surge cap to 150% of forecast requires a 6-month pilot MSA (we can draft).

Open questions for you:
- Do you want to include cross-account access for dashboards (we can add 3 guest seats at no incremental seat charge during pilot)?
- Would you prefer the pilot credit as a dollar credit or as incremental credits?

If you confirm we’ll prepare a short SOW + commercial appendix.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Principal Pricing Manager — Redwood Inference
Attachment: BRIGHTSIL-OBS-pricing_v1.pdf

From: Miguel Alvarez <miguel@brightsail.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability pack — retention / tracing questions

Thanks Kimberly — that matrix is helpful. A few follow-ups: 

1) On the credits slab: if BrightSail commits to 6 months at the suggested level, can Redwood guarantee that additional cold retention will not trigger a step-function price increase for incremental usage? Our workloads are bursty (e.g., model retrains), and CFO wants predictable marginal cost.

2) Guest seats: yes, please include 3 guest seats during pilot. If the pilot is successful we’ll likely expand to 20 seats — any volume discount?

3) Surge cap mechanics: For the 150% cap, can we get a daily alert when we cross 80% of forecasted spend so we can take action?

If you can confirm these points I’ll circulate to procurement and legal for an expedited PO.

Best,
Miguel

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Miguel Alvarez <miguel@brightsail.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability pack — retention / tracing questions

Miguel —

Quick answers to your follow-ups:

1) Price smoothing for incremental cold retention: We can include a marginal pricing ladder in the appendix: three incremental tiers with pre-agreed unit prices (no surprise step-function). The slabs you commit to will have priority allocation for cold archival so you get the lower blended unit until you exhaust the contracted bucket.

2) Seat discounting: For post-pilot expansion to 20 seats we can add a 10% seat discount in the commercial appendix tied to a 12-month seat commitment.

3) Spend alerts: Redwood’s console supports forecast alerts. We’ll enable a spend threshold webhook at 80% and 100% that can post to your ops@brightsail.ai Slack channel (we’ll include setup instructions in the SOW).

Action items we’ll execute this week:
- Ben: prepare a 1-page SOW stub + commercial appendix with the marginal ladder and seat discount term.
- Kimberly: include the worked numbers for the ladder in the pricing pdf.
- Miguel: confirm guest seat list and preferred PO approver for procurement.

I’m copying the DocuSign link once the SOW is ready.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
